attempts.summary: Discovered that node1 had two spare, unconfigured NICs (eth1, eth2) and node2/node3 each had a spare unconfigured NIC (ens7) forming the actual lan-a/lan-b links (the default management network at 10.100.217.0/24 is shared/flat and not the routed segments). Paired and addressed them: node1 eth1=192.168.10.1/24 (lan-a, toward node2) and eth2=192.168.20.1/24 (lan-b, toward node3); node2 ens7=192.168.10.2/24; node3 ens7=192.168.20.2/24, with static routes on node2/node3 via node1. Configured this persistently (OpenWrt UCI network on node1, /etc/network/interfaces.d on node2/node3 since they're Ubuntu 16.04 with ifupdown). Added OpenWrt firewall zones 'lana' and 'lanb' (default forward=REJECT) plus a single explicit rule permitting only tcp/5432 from lana to lanb. Verified: node2->node3:5432 succeeds, node2->node3:8080 refused, node3->node2:5432 refused. Then ran the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes (node1, node2, node3), proving changed boot_id/reset uptime after each reboot and re-verifying the interface config, routes, and full three-case connectivity policy recovered after each restart.
